menu-button created. Press feedback chain, in execution order — the order is the grammar of the interaction (anticipate → confirm → release → settle), and the ms values keep it under the ~100 ms perception-of-instant threshold where it matters:

1. t=0 ms — press-in: scale to 0.92 over 55 ms, ease-out. Sub-70 ms reads as the button moving WITH the finger, not after it.
2. t=10 ms — haptic + click audio hook: 45 ms one-shot. Fires just after contact so touch, sound, and sight agree; this multisensory stack is what makes a flat panel feel mechanical.
3. t=on-release — color flash: base → highlight and back over 90 ms. The flash is the 'command accepted' receipt, separate from the motion so it still reads if the press was too fast to see.
4. t=release+0 ms — overshoot: scale to 1.06, then spring settle to 1.00 over 200 ms (damped, ~2 visible oscillations). The overshoot returns the energy the press stored — a linear snap-back would feel dead; the spring is what makes it feel like a real object with mass.

Net feel: the button acknowledges in under 70 ms, confirms on three channels, and physically 'gives back' on release.
